newsitem.title: UK: Alumina prices seen stabilising as output rises.
newsitem.headline: Alumina prices seen stabilising as output rises.

text.p: Spot alumina prices should stabilise after dipping recently from peaks around $225 to $245 per tonne, Macquarie Equities said in a report.
Prices have eased to $215 to $225 per tonne fob due to rising output and a fall-off in Chinese buying. They should find an equilibrium in a $200-$240 range for the rest of 1997, it added.
"Capacity to produce alumina is adequate to meet any increase in demand from restarted aluminium smelting capacity," it said.
Production world-wide has increased following expansions in China and as most of Aluminum Co of America's (Alcoa) idled capacity has come back on stream, the broker said.
On the demand side, less interest has been seen from China, the main player in the spot market.
"This may partly be due to the new contract for 400,000 tonnes per year between the Chinese and Alcoa, which takes effect by mid-year," Macquarie said.
The spot market accounts for less than five percent of the total alumina market, but the spot price is a good indicator of overall market fundamentals, it added.
Most business is carried out on a fixed price or on the basis of LME prices.

Last week the International Primary Aluminium Institute (IPAI) released first quarter production statistics, but the raw data needed adjustments since it included for the first time figures from Kazakhstan and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Montenegro), Macquarie said.
Adjusted figures show a 2.4 percent rise in the first quarter of 1997 over the same period in 1996 to 10.305 million tonnes.
Increases in Alcoa's output had little effect, with Western production up only 100,000 tonnes. The biggest rise was in China and Eastern Europe.
Macquarie estimates a rise in Chinese output for full-year 1997 to 2.7-2.8 million tonnes from 2.5 million in 1996.
